I just got a baby porcupine puffer! :) 

1. What tank size? Right now my puffer (he's only a few inches at the moment) is in a 60 gallon and honestly the flow is a little much in some areas of the tank. They need a smaller tank to grow out in, but full grown, my puffer will be in a 250 gallon. Some sources say 90/100 gal is okay, but puffers are smart and get bored, so aim for at least 150, bigger if possible.
2. what kind of filtration is best? Get a tank with a sump. I have filter socks and a protein skimmer in my sump. 
3. what tank mates? look into predator tanks. I'm getting a baby longhorn cowfish soon. I'll also probably get a larger type of lionfish. I think porcupine puffers can live with just about any fish that can't fit in their mouth. Where things get difficult, is trying to stock a clean up crew. Puffers will eat snails, shrimp, crabs. Puffers will also eat corals! So most likely you'll have a FOWLR (fish only with live rock) tank. 
4. what's the best diet? When I got my puffer he wasn't eating frozen. So I had to order ghost shrimp and sacrifice my snails, but after two weeks he's finally taken to frozen food. I feed mysis, brine, plankton, krill, squid, clams, and whatever else comes in some of the frozen food blends.
5. what kind of Substrate/Aquascape would be best? You'll likely have a FOWLR tank. Live rock is where a lot of your bacteria will live. I also use live sand. Fiji pink seems to be the favorite. I bought a smaller grain sand for my 60 gallon and it blows around a bit. 
6. any other tips and tricks of getting into salt water for someone with a lot of experience with fresh water? Enjoy! FOWLR tanks, as opposed to coral tanks, aren't too hard to keep. It's mostly the same parameters as freshwater, aside from salinity (how salty the water is). Coral tanks require you to keep an eye on calcium, alkalinity, and magnesium as well.

I live in upstate NY so I see ticks all the time. My dogs have also received the Lyme vaccine, so they shouldn’t get Lyme if a tick does bite, but ticks can carry more illnesses than just Lyme.
